beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Adwait Changan, and this video is about the number that decides what counts as a problem. Today we are going to learn why I made my own finance agent unable to approve its own threshold. Every report this project has shipped flagged a variance as material. The number it used to decide that was a placeholder nobody had ever signed.

show.event: composer on cream; the fellow names himself and the subject
the ask types itself in, send button arms terracotta
running indicator: 'reading the build…'
three output lines land — what it decides, what mine was, what changed

props.command: What decides whether a variance is material, and who signed off on it?
output: A materiality threshold decides which variances get reported at all.
Mine was a demo fixture, marked unapproved, used in every run.
So the agent now structurally cannot be the one who approves it.

beats.narration_text: An approval has to carry three things or it is just a sentence. A name, so there is someone to ask. A stated basis, so the number is reasoned and not inherited. And the exact data it was judged against, so nobody can move the evidence afterwards and keep the signature.

show.event: 'A name' layer slides in
'A stated basis' stacks on
'The data it judged' lands in terracotta
caption underlines the failure it prevents

props.sparkLine: Three things, or it is a sentence.

layers.title: A name
layers.sub: someone you can go back and ask why

layers.title: A stated basis
layers.sub: the reasoning, not an inherited default

layers.title: The data it judged
layers.sub: hashed, so the evidence cannot move afterwards

props.caption: Miss the third and the signature outlives the thing it signed.

beats.narration_text: And here is what rested on it. Whether revenue was material. Whether cost of goods was material. Whether operating expenses were. Whether payroll was. Four judgements in every single report, all of them downstream of one number that said, in its own metadata, that nobody had approved it.

show.event: first chip lands as the voice names revenue
cost of goods lands
operating expenses lands
payroll completes the grid; caption names the common cause

props.caption: Every one of these was decided by a threshold marked DEMO_UNAPPROVED.

beats.narration_text: The obvious fix is to let the system approve it. Generate a record, mark it signed, move on. That is the failure I was actually designing against, because an agent that can approve its own threshold has not removed the judgement. It has just hidden who made it.

show.event: eyebrow ACT TWO draws in
serif title 'It Cannot Sign Its Own Work' types on
body copy fades up
spark line settles: 'Hidden, not removed.'

props.title: It Cannot Sign Its Own Work
props.body: An agent that approves its own threshold has not removed the judgement. It has hidden who made it.

beats.narration_text: So that is five lines. Read who signed it. If that name is one of the identities this system answers to, stop. Not a warning, not a flag on the report. The record is refused and nothing is written. The agent is allowed to prepare the request. It is never allowed to answer it.

show.event: Onda code block opens, filename in the title bar
the identity lookup writes on
the raise holds as the voice says 'stop'
the message is the last thing standing

props.title: materiality.py — the refusal

beats.narration_text: Run it four ways. The agent signs: refused. A human signs, but writes nothing that counts as a reason: refused. A named person with a stated basis: approved, and the name is on it. Then the same person signs again, and that is refused too, because an approval you can quietly replace is not evidence of anything.

show.event: the agent attempt writes on and is refused
the placeholder-reasoning attempt is refused
the named approval lands in terracotta
the duplicate attempt is refused last

artifactLines: agent signs it    ->  approved_by must be a named human, not the agent

beats.act: ACT 3 — WHAT A SIGNATURE IS WORTH
beats.narration_text: The binding is what makes it mean anything. The request records the hash of all six source files as the approver saw them. The decision carries those hashes back. And reading the approval later re-hashes the files on disk before the threshold is handed to anything.

show.event: 'Six source files' appears at the source position
the three binding steps light in narration order
arc completes toward the threshold
settle line: 'Change the data, lose the approval.'

props.destTitle: is released only if the data still matches
props.arcCaption: the signature is bound to evidence, not to a date
props.settleLine: Change the data, lose the approval.

beats.act: ACT 3 — WHAT A SIGNATURE IS WORTH
beats.narration_text: So here is the test that proves it is real rather than decorative. Record a valid approval. Then change one byte of the actuals file. Read the approval back and it refuses, naming the file that moved. The signature did not transfer to the new data, which is the only property that makes it worth having.

show.event: the recorded approval and its hash write on
'one byte of actuals.csv changes' lands
the refusal lands in terracotta, naming the file

props.artifactTitle: the test: does the signature transfer?
props.artifactHeading: A valid approval, then one byte changes
artifactLines: reading the approval back  ->  verified source changed since approval

beats.act: ACT 3 — WHAT A SIGNATURE IS WORTH
beats.narration_text: Which leaves a rule you can apply to anything that claims to be approved. Who is the name on it. What basis did they state. And what exact evidence were they looking at when they stated it. If the third answer is missing, the first two are decoration.

show.event: 'Who is the name?' slides in
'What basis did they state?' stacks on
'What were they looking at?' lands in terracotta
caption closes the rule

beats.act: ACT 3 — WHAT A SIGNATURE IS WORTH
beats.narration_text: And I shipped no approved threshold. The sample in the repository is a fixture and says so in its own reasoning field. A feature about named approval that ships with a fake signature would defeat itself on the first line.

show.event: eyebrow THE LIMIT draws in
serif title 'No Signature Is Shipped' types on
body copy fades up
spark line settles

props.title: No Signature Is Shipped
props.body: The sample in the repository is a fixture and says so in its own reasoning field. A feature about named approval cannot ship with an invented name.
props.sparkLine: A fixture, and it says so.

beats.narration_text: So, the verdict. The threshold that decided what counted as material was a demo fixture, and every report said so in its own metadata while using it anyway. It can now reach approved only through a record that names a human, states a basis of real length, and carries the hash of all six source files as that person saw them. The agent can prepare the request and is refused if it tries to answer it. Approvals are append-only, and reading one back re-hashes the data, so a signature cannot follow the evidence somewhere else. What it still does not do is tell you the amount is right.

show.event: verdict artifact page opens

the 'refused if it tries to sign' line holds in terracotta
the page settles complete

props.artifactHeading: A signature bound to evidence, or nothing
artifactLines: The threshold deciding materiality was a demo fixture, used in every report.
APPROVED now requires a named human, a stated basis, and the six source hashes.
The agent may prepare the request. It is refused if it tries to sign.
Approvals are append-only, and reading one back re-hashes the data first.
It records who decided and against what. It does not say the amount is right.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here is the prompt. Find every threshold, limit and cutoff in something I built. For each one tell me who chose the value, what reasoning was recorded, and what would break if it were wrong by a factor of two. Then tell me which ones are defaults nobody has ever examined. Run that on your own work. The last question is the one that stings, because a default you never chose is still a decision you are accountable for.

props.command: Find every threshold, limit and cutoff in this project. For each: who chose the value, what reasoning was recorded, and what breaks if it is wrong by a factor of two? Then tell me which are defaults nobody has examined.
output: Most thresholds in most systems were copied from an example and never revisited.
A default you never chose is still a decision you are accountable for.

beats.narration_text: That was the named materiality approval for the Mycroft Finance Investigator. The code and the tests are in pull request seventeen. Adwait Changan, for Humanitarians AI.
